- **godot-lsp**: GDScript code intelligence for Claude Code. Godot ships a real language server but only listens on TCP, while Claude Code runs every LSP server over stdio — its `transport: "socket"` option is accepted and then ignored, so the two never meet. This bridges them with a dependency-free 55-line pipe, giving hover, go-to-definition, find-references, symbols and diagnostics on .gd files from the engine's own analyser, built-in class documentation included. Requires the Godot editor to be open, since the language server lives in the editor rather than the engine. ([wfbcargo/blender-godot-plugins](https://github.com/wfbcargo/blender-godot-plugins/tree/HEAD/plugins/godot-lsp))

- **han-core**: The shared foundation of the Han suite: the specialist agent roster the other plugins dispatch, the project-discovery skill with its project-scanner agent, and the canonical evidence and YAGNI rule files. Note: NMI does NOT use Standard Webhooks — the Webhook-Signature header is "t=&lt;nonce&gt;,s=&lt;sig&gt;" (comma-separated) where t is a NONCE (not a Unix timestamp), and the signature is HMAC-SHA256 over "&lt;nonce&gt;.&lt;raw_body&gt;", lowercase hex. Covers the adapter seam (Transcriber/Generator), the prepare→run→score→diff CLI flow, the offline no-download smoke task, and how to interpret each metric. - **supertool**: Batch multiple file operations (read, grep, glob, ls, tail, head) into a single Bash round-trip. - **xpu-container-run**: Launch a Docker container with Intel GPU access on Linux. Encodes the correct combination of `--device /dev/dri`, render-group access, `--ipc=host`, `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` pinning, Hugging Face cache mount, and `--entrypoint /bin/bash` for interactive use. Use when running any Intel-XPU container (vLLM-XPU, sglang-xpu, torch-XPU, llama.cpp SYCL, etc.) and the device must be visible inside. The CUDA analogue is `docker run --gpus all` — Intel has no `--gpus` flag, you pass the Direct Rendering Manager (DRM) nodes directly. ([intel/gpu-ai-skills](https://github.com/intel/gpu-ai-skills/tree/HEAD/plugins/intel-gpu-ai-skills/skills/xpu-container-run))
- **xpu-deploy-plan**: Plan an end-to-end Intel XPU model deployment by chaining existing skills. Use when the user asks to deploy a model on an Intel GPU end-to-end, wants a single coordinated plan, or asks which skills to run and in what order. ([intel/gpu-ai-skills](https://github.com/intel/gpu-ai-skills/tree/HEAD/plugins/intel-gpu-ai-skills/skills/xpu-deploy-plan))
- **xpu-discover**: Inventory Intel GPUs (Arc, Arc Pro, Data Center GPU Max) on a Linux host. ([intel/gpu-ai-skills](https://github.com/intel/gpu-ai-skills/tree/HEAD/plugins/intel-gpu-ai-skills/skills/xpu-discover))
- **xpu-model-type-detect**: Detect whether a Hugging Face model is text generation, text encoder, seq2seq, masked LM, vision classification, vision-language (CLIP), audio encoder, audio seq2seq, multimodal VL, diffusion, time-series, or a reward model before loading it on Intel XPU. Pairs with torch-xpu-run and vllm-xpu-run so the agent picks the right AutoModel class and input kwargs and avoids wrong-input failures after a 20-second load. ([intel/gpu-ai-skills](https://github.com/intel/gpu-ai-skills/tree/HEAD/plugins/intel-gpu-ai-skills/skills/xpu-model-type-detect))
- **xpu-port**: Execute a single-target CUDA-to-XPU port of a PyTorch repo with libcst-based scan, mechanical rewrite, and CPU FP64 vs target-dtype correctness verify on one forward pass. Use when the request says "port" — "port my repo to XPU", "port my repo at &lt;path&gt; to XPU", "rewrite the CUDA calls to XPU", "apply the mechanical transforms", "run the scan and rewrite", "make the port changes now". Not for the "migrate" verb ("migrate my repo", "migrate this repo to XPU") or a bare whole-repo workflow request where scope is not yet set — those start with cuda-to-xpu-migration, whose plan routes here. Not f… ([intel/gpu-ai-skills](https://github.com/intel/gpu-ai-skills/tree/HEAD/plugins/intel-gpu-ai-skills/skills/xpu-port))
- **xpu-profile-unitrace**: Profile Intel-XPU workloads at the SYCL / Level Zero kernel level via Intel pti-gpu's unitrace. Captures per-API-call and per-kernel timing, memory transfers, oneCCL / MPI events, and hardware counters PyTorch-level profilers cannot see. Use when a hot op is already known at the torch.profiler layer and the user needs the SYCL kernel beneath, or when profiling oneCCL collectives in multi-GPU runs. Not for PyTorch-level signal (use torch-xpu-profile / vllm-xpu-profile). Requires building unitrace from source. ([intel/gpu-ai-skills](https://github.com/intel/gpu-ai-skills/tree/HEAD/plugins/intel-gpu-ai-skills/skills/xpu-profile-unitrace))
- **xpu-runtime-preflight**: Run a read-only go/no-go preflight before any Intel GPU/XPU skillpack work. Checks driver health, /dev/dri permissions, render/video groups, Docker, /dev/shm, disk, proxy, and optional container-level XPU visibility. Use when the user asks whether a machine is ready for XPU model work or needs a reusable lab readiness report. Not for launching workloads, pulling images, editing system config, or verifying model output. ([intel/gpu-ai-skills](https://github.com/intel/gpu-ai-skills/tree/HEAD/plugins/intel-gpu-ai-skills/skills/xpu-runtime-preflight))
- **xpu-system-setup**: First-time setup for Intel XPU/GPU hosts. Detects what's missing and installs xpu-smi, configures user groups (render), sets up Intel GPU PPA repository, installs Level Zero runtime, installs Docker, and runs a post-setup verification gate. Opt out per call with `[nosplit]` in the description, or session-wide with ALLOW_ZSH_NOSPLIT=1. ([filippolmt/skills](https://github.com/filippolmt/skills/tree/HEAD/plugins/zsh-wordsplit-guard))
